quote: Ch 17: Capability Proof must reference the 51 active MCP tools, health check protocols, and the proof-not-claims philosophy.

claim: Capability integration plan stresses capability manifests alongside confidence tracking.
quote: The integration callout links MCP tools to the capability manifest and VIF confidence tracking, reinforcing executable proof requirements.

claim: Quartet parity measures semantic alignment across code, docs, tests, and traces with threshold P >= 0.90.
Quartet elements defined: Code (source files), Docs (documentation), Tests (test files), Traces (execution traces).
Parity thresholds: Development P >= 0.85, Staging P >= 0.90, Production P >= 0.95.
Gate enforcement: Pre-commit gate, CI gate, deployment gate, quarantine system for changes with P < 0.90.
Capability is not a claim but a maintained proof. Every behavior has runnable evidence, fresh validation, and recorded confidence delta.
Capability ledger stored in CMC as atoms tagged 'capability' with fields: capability_id, description, owner, last_proved_at, proof_artifacts, vif_delta, status, next_audit_due.
Audit cadence: Tier S capabilities refresh every 24 hours, Tier A every 72 hours, Tier B every 7 days.
APOE refuses to execute chains requiring a capability if status != active.
CMC bitemporal storage enables 'what capabilities existed at time T?' queries for audit purposes.
SDF-CVF quartet parity formula: P = mean of 6 pairwise cosine similarities between code, docs, tests, traces.
CAS monitors capability drift and triggers automated audits based on tier cadence.
VIF updates confidence based on capability proof results, enabling confidence-based routing.
SEG links capability claims to supporting evidence anchors for validation.
